questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is an argument against government intervention when there is market failure?

options.A: Government intervention could increase positive externalities.
options.B: Government intervention could increase the availability of merit goods.
options.C: Government intervention could lead to a less efficient outcome.
options.D: Government intervention could reduce information failure.

questions.questionText: A government is choosing between four routes for a new road. The table provides details of the costs and benefits associated with each route. The government wants to get the highest return for taxpayers in terms of the social benefit relative to the private cost. Which route will the government choose? route ($ million) private private external costs benefits benefits

Donald maximises his utility when buying paperback books and audio books. The price of a paperback book = $3 and the price of an audio book = $6. If the marginal utility of the last paperback book was 12 units of utility (utils), what was the marginal utility of the last audio book purchased?

options.A: 2utils B 12utils C 16utils D 24utils

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the result of a price increase for an inferior good?

options.A: Both the substitution effect and the income effect cause the consumer to buy less of the good.
options.B: Both the substitution effect and the income effect cause the consumer to buy more of the good.
options.C: The substitution effect causes the consumer to buy less of the good and the income effect causes the consumer to buy more of the good.
options.D: The substitution effect causes the consumer to buy more of the good and the income effect causes the consumer to buy less of the good.

questions.questionText: Which statement about a monopoly is correct?

options.A: Profit maximisation occurs when average cost equals average revenue.
options.B: Sales maximisation occurs when marginal cost equals marginal revenue.
options.C: Sales revenue maximisation occurs when marginal revenue is equal to zero.
options.D: Satisficing occurs when marginal cost is equal to zero.

questions.questionText: A satellite communications company is bought by an investment bank. Which outcome has resulted from this purchase?

options.A: a cartel
options.B: diversification
options.C: lateral integration
options.D: vertical integration

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the long-run average cost (LRAC) curve for a firm, and three short-run average cost (SRAC) curves. cost SRAC1 $ LRAC SRAC2 SRAC3 O output Which statement is correct?

options.A: When the minimum point of SRAC3 is lower than the minimum point of SRAC2 it reflects the law of variable proportions.
options.B: The law of diminishing returns explains why each of the SRAC curves is U-shaped.
options.C: The position of SRAC2 shows the minimum efficient scale of production.
options.D: The rising section of SRAC1 indicates the existence of diseconomies of scale.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely reason that barriers to entry might lead to x-inefficiency?

options.A: The firm does not account for any external benefits.
options.B: The firm has no incentive to cut its costs of production.
options.C: The firm’s price is set higher than its average costs.
options.D: The firm’s price is set higher than its marginal costs.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the long-run cost and revenue curves for a public sector monopoly. revenue and costs AR LRAC MR LRMC O output The government decides to set a price that maximises social welfare. What will be the consequence of this decision?

options.A: The firm will experience diseconomies of scale.
options.B: The firm will make a loss.
options.C: The firm will maximise profits.
options.D: The firm will maximise total revenue.

questions.questionText: The information gives the characteristics for a market structure. ● The two leading brands control 60% of the market. ● Other large firms and a few smaller firms exist in the market. ● Prices tend to be stable. ● There are significant barriers to entry. Which market structure is this most likely to be?

options.A: monopolistic competition
options.B: monopoly
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm in imperfect competition. It changed its aim from profit maximising to sales revenue maximising. cost, MC revenue AC AR MR O output Which type of profit was it making in each case? profit sales revenue maximising maximising

options.A: normal profit supernormal profit
options.B: subnormal profit normal profit
options.C: supernormal profit normal profit
options.D: supernormal profit supernormal profit

questions.questionText: In various countries, the supply of public utilities such as water and electricity have been licensed by the government to a few private firms. What should governments do to persuade these profit-seeking private firms not to overcharge consumers?

options.A: allow private firms to merge to create a monopoly
options.B: appoint a regulatory body to guarantee supplies at all times
options.C: deregulate nationalised industries to create a free market
options.D: enable customers to switch easily from one private firm to another

questions.questionText: A government intends to use pollution permits to reduce environmental damage. Under what circumstances is this policy most likely to fail to achieve the intended reduction?

options.A: Firms within the scheme are required to have a sufficient number of permits to cover the amount of pollution generated in production.
options.B: Firms improve their technology to reduce the number of permits they require.
options.C: Firms that do not use all of their permits can sell some of them to other firms.
options.D: The permits do not impose strict enough limits on carbon emissions.

questions.questionText: A government is committed to reducing the Gini coefficient. Which policy is most likely to fail to achieve that policy objective?

options.A: a decrease in ad valorem sales tax rates
options.B: a more regressive income tax system
options.C: a more progressive income tax system
options.D: an increase in transfer payments to the unemployed

questions.questionText: Which calculation would give the marginal revenue product (MRP) of labour for a firm selling its product in an imperfectly competitive product market?

options.A: average output produced per worker employed  marginal revenue of the product
options.B: average output produced per worker employed  price of the product
options.C: extra product produced by an additional worker  marginal revenue of the product
options.D: extra product produced by an additional worker  price of the product

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the demand for and supply of labour in four markets.
Which objective would not be suitable for a government if it were seeking sustainable economic growth?

options.A: achieving the highest growth rate by using all the natural resources
options.B: careful management of the use of non-renewable resources
options.C: effective protection of the environment, wildlife and landscapes
options.D: meeting the needs of both its current and future population

questions.questionText: What is the difference between a country’s gross domestic product and its gross national income?

options.A: capital consumption
options.B: gross fixed capital formation
options.C: net property income from abroad
options.D: the value of exports less imports

questions.questionText: Some individuals seek to increase their share of existing wealth without creating new wealth. This can be a problem in developing economies. What is an example of this behaviour?

options.A: a government official taking a bribe for special treatment for the person offering the bribe
options.B: a land owner renting a field to a farmer
options.C: a landlord being paid for the hire of a room
options.D: an entrepreneur earning a reward for setting up a firm that pays low wages

questions.questionText: What is necessary to include to calculate the number unemployed? everyone of those of part-time employees working age who is pension age who seeking full-time not in employment still want to work employment

options.A: no no no
options.B: no yes yes
options.C: yes yes no
options.D: yes yes yes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows changes in the numbers employed in four different industries in a city between 2015 and 2020. employment finance (000) 50 manufacturing education leisure 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Finance was always the largest employer.
options.B: Leisure had the fastest growth rate in employment.
options.C: Manufacturing was the only industry to show signs of decline.
options.D: Total employment in the four industries decreased over the period.

questions.questionText: At the start of the year, the production possibility frontier for an economy is at PPF and the economy is at point S. At the end of the year the production possibility frontier is at PPF and the economy is at point T. Which diagram shows that the economy has experienced actual growth but not potential growth?

options.A: B output Y output Y S T T S PPF = PPF PPF PPF

Which change will allow an increase in an economy’s money supply?

options.A: An outflow of currency for trade and capital purposes becomes an inflow.
options.B: The central bank instructs commercial banks to keep higher ratios of cash to deposits.
options.C: The government budget balance moves from a deficit to a surplus.
options.D: The government replaces borrowing from the banks with borrowing from the general public.

questions.questionText: The UK gives aid to the Ugandan government to spend on a school. One condition is that they must buy the materials from the UK. Which type of aid does not take place?

options.A: bilateral
options.B: multilateral
options.C: project
options.D: tied

questions.questionText: Unemployment in an economy increases. What is a probable consequence?

options.A: a switch from direct to indirect taxation
options.B: an increase in demand-pull inflation
options.C: an increase in the balance of trade deficit
options.D: an increase in the government budget deficit

questions.questionText: The government of Lesotho introduces a programme to promote exports and to encourage firms to expand by subsidising local entrepreneurs. Which effect is this likely to have on incomes, the balance of payments current account deficit and government expenditure in Lesotho? balance of government incomes payments current expenditure account deficit

options.A: fall reduce rise
options.B: fall uncertain rise
options.C: rise reduce no change
options.D: rise uncertain rise
